title: tenant incubation and capacity silos for fast inference bootstrap
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated capacity experience variable cold-start latency during sudden traffic bursts. Existing warm pools reduce pain but are blunt: they pre-load whole model slices and compete across tenants, and autoscaling can be slow to honor SLA-backed throughput guarantees.

Goal: Implement an operator-driven 'tenant incubation' layer and capacity silos that reserve lightweight prewarmed slots tied to committed throughput. Incubation slots maintain small residency (partial weight residency + staged KV initialization) that can bootstrap full serving within strict SLO windows while allowing the autoscaler to react to sustained load. This ticket designs and implements the core orchestration, API knobs, and admission checks for the incubation/silo model, plus integration with throughput reservation and autoscale policy engine.

Key ideas:
- Tenanted incubation slots: soft reservations assigned per-tenant (or per-commit) that hold minimal memory-mapped weight shards and an initialized KV digest to accelerate first requests.
- Capacity silos: logical partitions of a GPU pool with guaranteed throughput tokens, preventing noisy-neighbor eviction during bursts.
- Staged bootstrap: three-phase start (digest probe -> partial weight stitch -> full residency) to balance memory and latency.
- Autoscaler-aware handoff: incubation hands over to full-serving instances when traffic persists; autoscaler uses a hysteresis aware of incubation usage to avoid overprovisioning.

This ticket covers design, implementation of controller, admission + quota API, minimal runtime surface for partial residency, and end-to-end validation in canary fleet.
acceptance_criteria: API to create/consume incubation slots (internal opt-in) implemented and documented in the console API catalog
Controller assigns incubation slots honoring tenant throughput reservations within 2s for eligible burst events in synthetic tests
Partial residency reduces 95th percentile cold-start token latency by >=40% compared to cold baseline in the dedicated canary cluster
Capacity silo enforcement prevents eviction of incubation slots for reserved tenants under synthetic cross-tenant stress
Autoscaler consumes incubation signals and performs handoff without duplicative weight loads (observed single full-load per handoff)
Integration tests, e2e perf dashboards, and a migration doc for Dedicated customers are published
technical_notes: Incubation slot model: store lightweight mmap of key transformer blocks (first N layers) and stream-in remaining layers on demand. Use LRU-backed ephemeral slices to bound memory.

KV digest probe: calculate a small representative set of KV keys (profiled from recent traffic or tenant-provided head prompts) and prepopulate a fast in-RAM index to prime KV cache hits for prefix-heavy workloads.
Silo token accounting: extend existing capacity ledger to include token buckets per-silo; tokens correspond to commit throughput and decay over rolling 1-hour windows for burst headroom.
Admission logic: prefer assigning incubation slots to tenants with active SLAs and recent traffic; fall back to shared warm pool if no commitments.
Handoff: expose a graceful takeover protocol where a full-serving replica marks 'bootstrapping' and borrows the incision slot's KV digest to avoid redundant probes.
Observability: add metrics incubation_slot_alloc, incubation_slot_eviction_reason, silo_token_balance, incubation_handoff_latency, kv_digest_hitrate
Trade-offs considered: full preloading reduces initial variance but adds memory cost; staged residency uses modest memory and may still see a few increased tokens for worst-case long prompts.
rollout_plan: Week 0: merge design PR and controller prototype behind feature flag (internal-only)
Week 1: unit/integration tests, add metrics, and synthetic perf harness for cold-start comparisons
Week 2: deploy to dedicated canary cluster (1 server per region) and run steady-state + burst tests for targeted tenants
Week 3: open alpha to select customers with committed reserved capacity and collect SLA telemetry
Week 4: run a 72-hour stress with cross-tenant noise to validate siloing; if pass, promote feature flag to broad Dedicated clusters
Post-rollout: adjust default incubation size parameters and publish migration/playbook for customers
dependencies_notes: Depends on kernel scheduling improvements in ENG-110234 for partial-weight mapping performance; coordination with background hydration tasks from ENG-30512 to avoid double-loading
risks: If silo token accounting is too permissive, noisy tenants could still starve incubations; will mitigate with eviction scoring and tenant throttles
Partial residency adds complexity to runtime; regression tests required to ensure KV coherency during handoff
Incorrect KV digest sampling can bias priming and not help real traffic; will build sampling validation harness

2025-11-30 - Liam Chen: Added preliminary metrics and feature flag gate in the controller. Deployed to dev cluster behind flag and ran synthetic bursts; KV digest hitrate varies based on prompt diversity — added opt-in tenant-provided sample prompts to improve hitrate.
